CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regency is Muara Enim Regency. 2. Regency Government is Muara Enim Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Muara Enim. 4. Regional Apparatus is the Regional Apparatus within the Muara Enim Regency Government. 5. Women's Empowerment is the strengthening of human rights, enhancement of Protection efforts, quality of life, and increased participation of women in development. 6. Women's Protection is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred; 7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive Protection from Violence and discrimination. 7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb and has not married. 8. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and Children. 9. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of a person's freedom unlawfully. 10. Children's Forum is a forum for Child participation formed with the aim of facilitating the involvement of Children in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity. 11. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a Child rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. 12. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies. 13. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 14. Women Victims of Violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 15. Child Victims of Violence are Children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 16. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of Violence, use of Violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 17. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of Violence against women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 18. Social rehabilitation is services aimed at restoring and developing the abilities of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions normally. 19. Law enforcement is the action of officers authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 20. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of Violence against women and Children that are gender sensitive. 21. Repatriation is an effort to return women and Child victims of Violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving Region to the Region of origin. 22. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 23. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide Protection and a sense of security to victims of Violence. 24. Shelter house is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 25. Spiritual Guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 26. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of development policies, programs, and activities in the Region. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28. Gender Sensitivity or Gender Awareness is the ability to identify gaps in power relations between women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on women and men, and the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of women and men are different. 29.

Article 82

The family in efforts to protect women's rights has the role of:
a. protecting women from conflict and domestic violence that degrades the dignity of women;
b. providing equal opportunities for women to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political and cultural affairs; and
c. preventing violations of women's rights in the household.

Article 21

1. Victim assistance, law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in Article 13 letter d constitute actions by law enforcement officials to implement laws and regulations in handling cases of acts of violence against women, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.
2. Victim assistance, law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of victims.

CHAPTER IX

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 84

1. The Regency Government is obliged to conduct guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence.
2. Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:
a. guidelines and fulfillment standards;
b. technical guidance and training;
c. provision of facilities;
d. monitoring; and
e. evaluation.
3. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (2) in order to realize the objectives of protection for women and children victims of violence in accordance with minimum service standards implemented by the agency in charge of Women and Children Protection.
4. The agency in charge of Women and Children Protection is obliged to report periodically to the Regent regarding the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence.

Article 19

1. The Regency Government may provide safe houses for women victims of acts of violence.
2. The provision of safe house services as referred to in Article 17 paragraph (2) letter b aims to protect women victims of acts of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.
3. The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
4. Criteria for women victims of acts of violence who require safe houses include:
a. life-threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or
d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.
4. The provision of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of:
a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and/or
c. community leaders.
5. Further provisions regarding the provision of safe house services shall be regulated in a Regent Regulation.

Article 15

1. Complaints of acts of violence against women may be made by reporters consisting of:
a. victims;
b. family;
c. community; and/or
d. community organizations in the field of protection of women and children.
2. Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may make complaints:
a. directly;
b. by telephone; and/or
c. by letter.
3. In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, the agency responsible for the Protection of Women and Children, officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 13, are also authorized to provide assistance in handling victims of acts of violence against women obtained through other information.
4. Further provisions regarding procedures for complaint handling services as referred to in paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 71

Special protection for child victims of physical and/or psychological violence as referred to in Article 60 paragraph (1) letter i shall be carried out through efforts: (36)
a. dissemination and socialization of the provisions of Laws and Regulations that protect child victims of acts of violence; and
b. monitoring, reporting, and imposition of sanctions.

Article 24

1. Social reintegration is carried out in order to reunite women victims of violence with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
2. Social reintegration is intended so that:
a. women victims of violence can resume their social life; and
b. women victims of violence can have a decent life.
3. Social reintegration as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out after the victim receives social rehabilitation services.

CHAPTER III

PROTECTION OF WOMEN

Part One

General

Part Two

Prevention of Acts of Violence Against Women

Article 42

1. The Regency Government is obliged to provide comprehensive health services for children, so that every Child obtains optimal health status from the womb.
2. Comprehensive health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative efforts for basic health services;
b. exemption from cost burdens for malnourished Children, children with disabilities, children with special needs, children infected with HIV/AIDS, child workers, children victims of narcotics abuse, alcohol, psychotropics and other addictive substances, children who are victims of violence, and child victims of human trafficking; and
3. The Regency Government, community, family and parents are obliged to ensure that children born are protected from diseases that threaten the continuity of life and/or cause disability.

Article 40

1. Every child has the right to obtain education and teaching in the context of developing their personality and level of intelligence in accordance with their interests and talents.
2. Every child has the right to receive protection in education units from sexual crimes and violence committed by educators, education personnel, fellow students, and/or other parties.

Law enforcement is the action of officers authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 20. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of Violence against women and Children that are gender sensitive. 21. Repatriation is an effort to return women and Child victims of Violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving Region to the Region of origin. 22. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 23. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide Protection and a sense of security to victims of Violence. 24. Shelter house is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 25. Spiritual Guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 26. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of development policies, programs, and activities in the Region. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28. Gender Sensitivity or Gender Awareness is the ability to identify gaps in power relations between women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on women and men, and the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of women and men are different. 29.

Article 40

1. Every child has the right to obtain education and teaching in the context of developing their personality and level of intelligence in accordance with their interests and talents.
2. Every child has the right to receive protection in education units from sexual crimes and violence committed by educators, education personnel, fellow students, and/or other parties.

CHAPTER IX

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 84

1. The Regency Government is obliged to conduct guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence.
2. Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:
a. guidelines and fulfillment standards;
b. technical guidance and training;
c. provision of facilities;
d. monitoring; and
e. evaluation.
3. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (2) in order to realize the objectives of protection for women and children victims of violence in accordance with minimum service standards implemented by the agency in charge of Women and Children Protection.
4. The agency in charge of Women and Children Protection is obliged to report periodically to the Regent regarding the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence.

Article 19

1. The Regency Government may provide safe houses for women victims of acts of violence.
2. The provision of safe house services as referred to in Article 17 paragraph (2) letter b aims to protect women victims of acts of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.
3. The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
4. Criteria for women victims of acts of violence who require safe houses include:
a. life-threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or
d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.
4. The provision of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of:
a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and/or
c. community leaders.
5. Further provisions regarding the provision of safe house services shall be regulated in a Regent Regulation.

Part Two

Prevention of Acts of Violence Against Women

Article 42

1. The Regency Government is obliged to provide comprehensive health services for children, so that every Child obtains optimal health status from the womb.
2. Comprehensive health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative efforts for basic health services;
b. exemption from cost burdens for malnourished Children, children with disabilities, children with special needs, children infected with HIV/AIDS, child workers, children victims of narcotics abuse, alcohol, psychotropics and other addictive substances, children who are victims of violence, and child victims of human trafficking; and
3. The Regency Government, community, family and parents are obliged to ensure that children born are protected from diseases that threaten the continuity of life and/or cause disability.

Article 68

1. Every Person is obliged to protect children from the influence of pornography and prevent children's access to information containing pornographic elements.
2. Special Protection for children who are victims of pornography as referred to in Article 60 paragraph (1) letter f shall be implemented through guidance, assistance, and social, physical and mental health recovery efforts.
3. Guidance, assistance, and social, physical and mental health recovery as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

Article 15

1. Complaints of acts of violence against women may be made by reporters consisting of:
a. victims;
b. family;
c. community; and/or
d. community organizations in the field of protection of women and children.
2. Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may make complaints:
a. directly;
b. by telephone; and/or
c. by letter.
3. In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, the agency responsible for the Protection of Women and Children, officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 13, are also authorized to provide assistance in handling victims of acts of violence against women obtained through other information.
4. Further provisions regarding procedures for complaint handling services as referred to in paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 21

1. Victim assistance, law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in Article 13 letter d constitute actions by law enforcement officials to implement laws and regulations in handling cases of acts of violence against women, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.
2. Victim assistance, law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of victims.

Article 39

1. Every education unit organizer is obliged to provide opportunities for children to obtain educational services without discrimination.
2. Every education unit organizer is prohibited from expelling children from educational institutions unless there is a guarantee for the continuity of the child's education.
3. In the event that a child victim of Violence experiences dropping out of school, the education unit organizer is obliged to coordinate with relevant agencies.

Article 20

1. Spiritual guidance as referred to in Article 17 paragraph (2) letter d aims for psychological recovery.
2. Spiritual guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented based on the principles of:
a. not imposing any religion or belief; and
b. leaving the final decision in the hands of the victim (self determination).
3. Spiritual guidance is provided by spiritual guidance officers.
4. Spiritual guidance officers as referred to in paragraph (3) consist of consultants from the Advisory Board for Marriage Guidance and Preservation, Officers of the Office of Religious Affairs, Ustads/Islamic Scholars, Priests, Pastors and other religious leaders who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness.

Article 19

3. In every formulation of policies related to children, the Regional Government must consider and accommodate the opinions of children submitted through the children's participation forum.
4. Further provisions regarding the establishment of the Children's Forum as referred to in paragraph (1) through paragraph (3) shall be stipulated by Regent's Decree.

b. exemption from cost burdens for malnourished Children, children with disabilities, children with special needs, children infected with HIV/AIDS, child workers, children victims of narcotics abuse, alcohol, psychotropics and other addictive substances, children who are victims of violence, and child victims of human trafficking; and

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb and has not married. 8. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of a person's freedom unlawfully. 10. Children's Forum is a forum for Child participation formed with the aim of facilitating the involvement of Children in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity. 11. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a Child rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. 12. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies. 13. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 14. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of Violence against women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 18. Social rehabilitation is services aimed at restoring and developing the abilities of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions normally. 19. Law enforcement is the action of officers authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 20. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of Violence against women and Children that are gender sensitive. 21. Repatriation is an effort to return women and Child victims of Violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving Region to the Region of origin. 22. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 23. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide Protection and a sense of security to victims of Violence. 24. Shelter house is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 25. Spiritual Guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 26. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of development policies, programs, and activities in the Region. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28. Gender Sensitivity or Gender Awareness is the ability to identify gaps in power relations between women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on women and men, and the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of women and men are different. 29.

Social rehabilitation is services aimed at restoring and developing the abilities of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions normally. 19. Law enforcement is the action of officers authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 20. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of Violence against women and Children that are gender sensitive. 21. Repatriation is an effort to return women and Child victims of Violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving Region to the Region of origin. 22. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 23. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide Protection and a sense of security to victims of Violence. 24. Shelter house is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 25. Spiritual Guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 26. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of development policies, programs, and activities in the Region. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28. Gender Sensitivity or Gender Awareness is the ability to identify gaps in power relations between women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on women and men, and the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of women and men are different. 29.

Article 24

1. Social reintegration is carried out in order to reunite women victims of violence with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
2. Social reintegration is intended so that:
a. women victims of violence can resume their social life; and
b. women victims of violence can have a decent life.
3. Social reintegration as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out after the victim receives social rehabilitation services.

Part Three

Effectiveness of Services for Women Victims of Acts of Violence

Article 21

1. Victim assistance, law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in Article 13 letter d constitute actions by law enforcement officials to implement laws and regulations in handling cases of acts of violence against women, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.
2. Victim assistance, law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of victims.

Article 82

The family in efforts to protect women's rights has the role of:
a. protecting women from conflict and domestic violence that degrades the dignity of women;
b. providing equal opportunities for women to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political and cultural affairs; and
c. preventing violations of women's rights in the household.

Article 19

1. The Regency Government may provide safe houses for women victims of acts of violence.
2. The provision of safe house services as referred to in Article 17 paragraph (2) letter b aims to protect women victims of acts of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.
3. The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
4. Criteria for women victims of acts of violence who require safe houses include:
a. life-threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or
d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.
4. The provision of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of:
a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and/or
c. community leaders.
5. Further provisions regarding the provision of safe house services shall be regulated in a Regent Regulation.

Article 84

1. The Regency Government is obliged to conduct guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence.

Article 25

The Regency Government implements repatriation and social reintegration of women victims of violence in accordance with laws and regulations.

Article 15

1. Complaints of acts of violence against women may be made by reporters consisting of:
a. victims;
b. family;
c. community; and/or
d. community organizations in the field of protection of women and children.

a. directly;
b. by telephone; and/or
c. by letter.
3. In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, the agency responsible for the Protection of Women and Children, officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 13, are also authorized to provide assistance in handling victims of acts of violence against women obtained through other information.
4. Further provisions regarding procedures for complaint handling services as referred to in paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 23

1. Repatriation is intended to return women victims of violence to their region of origin.
2. Repatriation of women victims of violence is accompanied by social reintegration efforts.

CHAPTER IX

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 84

1. The Regency Government is obliged to conduct guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence.
2. Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:
a. guidelines and fulfillment standards;
b. technical guidance and training;
c. provision of facilities;
d. monitoring; and
e. evaluation.
3. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (2) in order to realize the objectives of protection for women and children victims of violence in accordance with minimum service standards implemented by the agency in charge of Women and Children Protection.
4. The agency in charge of Women and Children Protection is obliged to report periodically to the Regent regarding the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence.

Article 39

1. Every education unit organizer is obliged to provide opportunities for children to obtain educational services without discrimination.
2. Every education unit organizer is prohibited from expelling children from educational institutions unless there is a guarantee for the continuity of the child's education.
3. In the event that a child victim of Violence experiences dropping out of school, the education unit organizer is obliged to coordinate with relevant agencies.

Article 63

Special protection for child victims of riots, disaster victims, and children in armed conflict as referred to in Article 61 paragraph (1) letter b, letter c, and letter d, shall be implemented through:
a. fulfillment of basic needs consisting of food, clothing, housing, education, health, learning and recreation, security guarantees, and equal treatment; and
b. fulfillment of special needs for children with disabilities and children experiencing psychosocial disorders.

Article 80

1. Community participation in efforts to protect women and children:
a. participate in prevention and provide support for the development of prevention programs for violations of the rights of women and children;
b. provide information and/or report violations of the rights of women and children to the competent authorities; andc. supervise the law enforcement process for cases of violations of the rights of women and children.
2. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be based on laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

Article 21

1. Victim assistance, law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in Article 13 letter d constitute actions by law enforcement officials to implement laws and regulations in handling cases of acts of violence against women, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.
2. Victim assistance, law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of victims.

Article 71

Special protection for child victims of physical and/or psychological violence as referred to in Article 60 paragraph (1) letter i shall be carried out through efforts: (36)
a. dissemination and socialization of the provisions of Laws and Regulations that protect child victims of acts of violence; and
b. monitoring, reporting, and imposition of sanctions.

Article 15

1. Complaints of acts of violence against women may be made by reporters consisting of:
a. victims;
b. family;
c. community; and/or
d. community organizations in the field of protection of women and children.
2. Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may make complaints:
a. directly;
b. by telephone; and/or
c. by letter.
3. In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, the agency responsible for the Protection of Women and Children, officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 13, are also authorized to provide assistance in handling victims of acts of violence against women obtained through other information.
4. Further provisions regarding procedures for complaint handling services as referred to in paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 19

1. The Regency Government may provide safe houses for women victims of acts of violence.
2. The provision of safe house services as referred to in Article 17 paragraph (2) letter b aims to protect women victims of acts of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.

b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or

Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive Protection from Violence and discrimination. 7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb and has not married. 8. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and Children. 9. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of a person's freedom unlawfully. 10. Children's Forum is a forum for Child participation formed with the aim of facilitating the involvement of Children in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity. 11. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a Child rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. 12. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies. 13. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 14. Women Victims of Violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 15. Child Victims of Violence are Children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 16. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of Violence, use of Violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 17. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of Violence against women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 18. Social rehabilitation is services aimed at restoring and developing the abilities of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions normally. 19. Law enforcement is the action of officers authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 20. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of Violence against women and Children that are gender sensitive. 21. Repatriation is an effort to return women and Child victims of Violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving Region to the Region of origin. 22. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 23. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide Protection and a sense of security to victims of Violence. 24. Shelter house is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 25. Spiritual Guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 26. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of development policies, programs, and activities in the Region. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28. Gender Sensitivity or Gender Awareness is the ability to identify gaps in power relations between women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on women and men, and the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of women and men are different. 29.

1. Community participation in efforts to protect women and children:
a. participate in prevention and provide support for the development of prevention programs for violations of the rights of women and children;
b. provide information and/or report violations of the rights of women and children to the competent authorities; andc. supervise the law enforcement process for cases of violations of the rights of women and children.

Part Two

Prevention of Acts of Violence Against Women

Article 15

1. Complaints of acts of violence against women may be made by reporters consisting of:
a. victims;
b. family;
c. community; and/or
d. community organizations in the field of protection of women and children.

a. directly;
b. by telephone; and/or

3. In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, the agency responsible for the Protection of Women and Children, officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 13, are also authorized to provide assistance in handling victims of acts of violence against women obtained through other information.

Article 19

1. The Regency Government may provide safe houses for women victims of acts of violence.
2. The provision of safe house services as referred to in Article 17 paragraph (2) letter b aims to protect women victims of acts of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.

PROTECTION OF WOMEN

Part One

General

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regency is Muara Enim Regency. 2. Regency Government is Muara Enim Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Muara Enim. 4. Regional Apparatus is the Regional Apparatus within the Muara Enim Regency Government. 5. Women's Empowerment is the strengthening of human rights, enhancement of Protection efforts, quality of life, and increased participation of women in development. 6. Women's Protection is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred; 7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive Protection from Violence and discrimination. 7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb and has not married. 8. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and Children. 9. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of a person's freedom unlawfully. 10. Children's Forum is a forum for Child participation formed with the aim of facilitating the involvement of Children in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity. 11. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a Child rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. 12. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies. 13. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 14. Women Victims of Violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 15. Child Victims of Violence are Children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 16. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of Violence, use of Violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 17. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of Violence against women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 18. Social rehabilitation is services aimed at restoring and developing the abilities of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions normally. 19. Law enforcement is the action of officers authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 20. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of Violence against women and Children that are gender sensitive. 21. Repatriation is an effort to return women and Child victims of Violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving Region to the Region of origin. 22. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 23. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide Protection and a sense of security to victims of Violence. 24. Shelter house is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 25. Spiritual Guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 26. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of development policies, programs, and activities in the Region. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28. Gender Sensitivity or Gender Awareness is the ability to identify gaps in power relations between women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on women and men, and the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of women and men are different. 29.

Article 19

1. The Regency Government may provide safe houses for women victims of acts of violence.
2. The provision of safe house services as referred to in Article 17 paragraph (2) letter b aims to protect women victims of acts of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.
3. The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
4. Criteria for women victims of acts of violence who require safe houses include:
a. life-threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or
d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.
4. The provision of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of:
a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and/or
c. community leaders.
5. Further provisions regarding the provision of safe house services shall be regulated in a Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER IX

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 84

1. The Regency Government is obliged to conduct guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence.
2. Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:
a. guidelines and fulfillment standards;
b. technical guidance and training;
c. provision of facilities;
d. monitoring; and
e. evaluation.
3. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (2) in order to realize the objectives of protection for women and children victims of violence in accordance with minimum service standards implemented by the agency in charge of Women and Children Protection.
4. The agency in charge of Women and Children Protection is obliged to report periodically to the Regent regarding the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence.

Article 21

1. Victim assistance, law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in Article 13 letter d constitute actions by law enforcement officials to implement laws and regulations in handling cases of acts of violence against women, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.
2. Victim assistance, law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of victims.

Part Three

Improvement of the Role, Quality, and Capacity of Women in the Legal Field

Article 82

The family in efforts to protect women's rights has the role of:
a. protecting women from conflict and domestic violence that degrades the dignity of women;
b. providing equal opportunities for women to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political and cultural affairs; and
c. preventing violations of women's rights in the household.

Article 80

1. Community participation in efforts to protect women and children:
a. participate in prevention and provide support for the development of prevention programs for violations of the rights of women and children;
b. provide information and/or report violations of the rights of women and children to the competent authorities; andc. supervise the law enforcement process for cases of violations of the rights of women and children.
2. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be based on laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

Article 23

1. Repatriation is intended to return women victims of violence to their region of origin.
2. Repatriation of women victims of violence is accompanied by social reintegration efforts.

Improvement of the Role, Quality and Capacity of Women in the Political Field

Paragraph 1

Part Four

Improvement of the Role, Quality, and Capacity of Women in the Social Field

Article 24

1. Social reintegration is carried out in order to reunite women victims of violence with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
2. Social reintegration is intended so that:
a. women victims of violence can resume their social life; and
b. women victims of violence can have a decent life.
3. Social reintegration as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out after the victim receives social rehabilitation services.

CHAPTER X

FINANCING

Article 85 Financing for the implementation of programs and activities for the Protection of Women and Children is sourced from:
a. regional revenue and expenditure budget; and
b. other legitimate sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Paragraph 5

Victim Assistance, Law Enforcement and Legal Aid

Public service providers are every state organizing institution, corporation, independent institution formed based on Law for public service activities, and other legal entities formed solely for public service activities. 30. Community Organizations are organizations established and formed by the community voluntarily based on common aspirations, will, needs, interests, activities and goals to participate in development for the achievement of the goals of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila. 31. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 32. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband, wife and their Child, or father and his Child, or mother and her Child, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree. 33. Customs are eternal patterns of behavior passed down from one generation to another generation as heritage, so that they are strongly integrated with community behavior patterns. 32. Best interests are the best interests for women and children.

Part Three

Improvement of the Role, Quality, and Capacity of Women in the Legal Field

Article 21

1. Victim assistance, law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in Article 13 letter d constitute actions by law enforcement officials to implement laws and regulations in handling cases of acts of violence against women, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.
2. Victim assistance, law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of victims.

Article 66

Special Protection for children who are exploited economically and/or sexually as referred to in Article 60 paragraph (1) letter d shall be carried out through:
a. dissemination and/or socialization of the provisions of Laws and Regulations related to the protection of children who are exploited economically and/or sexually.
b. involvement of various companies, labor unions, Non-Governmental Organizations, and the community in the elimination of economic and/or sexual exploitation of children.

Article 68

1. Every Person is obliged to protect children from the influence of pornography and prevent children's access to information containing pornographic elements.
2. Special Protection for children who are victims of pornography as referred to in Article 60 paragraph (1) letter f shall be implemented through guidance, assistance, and social, physical and mental health recovery efforts.
3. Guidance, assistance, and social, physical and mental health recovery as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

Article 53

1. In organizing the fulfillment of children's rights to express opinions and participate, the Regency Government facilitates the establishment of a Children's Forum.
2. The Children's Forum as referred to in paragraph (1) represents children in the Region, both representing the geographical domicile of children, components of children's socio-cultural groups and children's educational backgrounds.
3. In every formulation of policies related to children, the Regional Government must consider and accommodate the opinions of children submitted through the children's participation forum.
4. Further provisions regarding the establishment of the Children's Forum as referred to in paragraph (1) through paragraph (3) shall be stipulated by Regent's Decree.

Part Four

Improvement of the Role, Quality, and Capacity of Women in the Social Field

CHAPTER IV

IMPROVING FAMILY QUALITY

Article 28

1. In order to improve the quality of family life, the Regency Government is responsible for:
a. making efforts to improve family quality to realize gender equality and children's rights;
b. providing services for families in realizing gender equality and children's rights; and
c. strengthening and developing service provider institutions for improving family quality in the Regency.
2. The responsibility of the Regency Government in efforts to improve family quality as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented by regional apparatus in accordance with their duties and functions.

CHAPTER IV

IMPROVING FAMILY QUALITY

Article 28

1. In order to improve the quality of family life, the Regency Government is responsible for:
a. making efforts to improve family quality to realize gender equality and children's rights;
b. providing services for families in realizing gender equality and children's rights; and
c. strengthening and developing service provider institutions for improving family quality in the Regency.
2. The responsibility of the Regency Government in efforts to improve family quality as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented by regional apparatus in accordance with their duties and functions.

Article 41

1. Children with disabilities and children with special needs are given equal opportunities to obtain formal, non-formal and informal educational services, including inclusive education programs.
2. The Regency Government provides teaching staff for inclusive education at every education unit.
